name: Hidden Threat: North Korean IT Workers Exposed

attribution.legal_posture: Publisher-attributed public research finding; legal adjudication and civil identity require separate evidence.

caveats: Attribution is KELA’s assessment; the record carries a research attribution.
Infostealer contents, credentials, identity-document images, personal photographs, raw emails, wallet selectors, and victim/client details remain unpublished.
The operator remains unnamed in this dataset.

statements: KELA reports an unnamed suspected DPRK operator seeking architecture, structural-engineering, industrial-design and interior-design work, expanding the hiring-risk model beyond conventional software roles.

The report describes a structured persona-management workflow using a multi-profile browser, separate email purposes, translation, proxies and cryptocurrency, plus repositories used to stage résumé and proposal material.

The public article says identity-editing resources and platform-specific folders were organized at scale; this supports a persona-factory TTP but not publication of the underlying IDs, credentials, photographs or victim data.
